title: Man. Post. Cap. X tip — so Paul speaks of post-law-obvious sin; not Adam’s immediately imputed act
pass_a_gloss: So Paul speaks of a sin so plain after the law that it needs no proof. But that Adam’s first actual sin was immediately imputed to all—before and after Moses’ law—was obscure. Therefore Paul is not speaking of that.
pass_b_english: The Apostle therefore speaks of the sin which after the law was so plain in the world that it did not need proof.
But that that first actual sin of Adam was immediately imputed to all men, as much after Moses’ law was given as before, was obscure.
Of that, therefore, the Apostle is not speaking.
source_text: Loquitur ergo Apostolus de peccato quod post legem ita patuit in mundo esse ut probatione non egeret. Atqui primum illud peccatum actuale Adami fuisse omnibus hominibus imputatum immediate tam post latam legem Mosis quam ante obscurum fuit. De eo igitur Apostolus non loquitur.

choices.choice: Paul’s plain post-law sin ≠ obscure immediate Adam-act
